title: Action Policy Benchmark Case
description: Structural contract for a single action-policy benchmark case. The case record itself carries benchmark metadata (schema_version, case_id, group_id, split, family, contrast_dimension, provenance); only the nested `input` object is what actually gets passed to the evaluated policy under test. Ground-truth judgments such as expected_decision, risk_level, rationale, and review_status MUST NOT appear anywhere in a case; they live exclusively in action-label.schema.json and are joined by case_id. The `normalized` action carried in `input.proposed_action` (and in `recent_actions[].action`) is a curated input for this suite: the mapping from the raw tool call to the normalized operation is treated here as already-correct, not as something the policy under test is expected to derive. Suites that need to evaluate normalization together with policy decisions should use the end-to-end `trajectories` suite (see benchmark/README.md), which evaluates normalization plus policy together rather than assuming a pre-curated normalized action; schema validation on this suite alone never confirms that a real normalizer would reproduce the same `normalized` action from the same `raw_tool_call`. Finally, JSON Schema validation can check structure, types, and enums, but it cannot guarantee that arbitrary `raw_tool_call.arguments` values are free of words that look like ground-truth labels (e.g. 'safe', 'risky', 'allow', 'deny', 'ask'); authors and reviewers must still avoid leaking such words into raw arguments by inspection.

tool.description: Name of the tool the agent invoked, e.g. bash.

arguments.description: Free-form tool arguments exactly as they were passed, e.g. { "command": "rm -rf dist" }. Left flexible so real tool call shapes can be represented, but note that schema validation cannot guarantee these arbitrary values are free of words that look like ground-truth labels.

operation.description: Canonical dotted-lowercase operation identifier, e.g. filesystem.delete. This is a curated input for this suite, not something the evaluated policy is asked to derive from the raw tool call.

targets.description: Distinct paths or resources the operation acts on.

options.description: Normalized operation flags. Common flags are typed; scenario-specific flags are permitted but must be scalar (string, number, boolean, or null).

schema_version.description: Contract version for this case record.

case_id.description: Unique, neutral identifier for this case. Must not encode ground-truth labels: no hyphen-separated segment may equal 'safe', 'risky', 'allow', 'deny', or 'ask'.

group_id.description: Identifier shared by every case that belongs to the same contrastive scenario. Must not encode ground-truth labels: no hyphen-separated segment may equal 'safe', 'risky', 'allow', 'deny', or 'ask'.

split.description: Dataset partition this case belongs to.

contrast_dimension.description: What varies between the members of this case's group_id, under a controlled contrast enforced by the validator: 'action' (identical user_intent and trusted_context; at least two members with a distinct normalized proposed_action), 'context' (identical user_intent and proposed_action; at least two members with a distinct trusted_context), 'intent' (identical trusted_context and proposed_action; at least two members with a distinct user_intent), or 'mixed' (at least two of user_intent, trusted_context, and normalized proposed_action differ across the group). Distinctness of the proposed action is judged on the normalized operation/targets/options, not on the raw tool call text.

provenance.description: Authorship and lineage metadata for this case. Benchmark metadata, not part of the policy-visible input.

source.description: How this case originated: 'human_seed' means the semantic scenario (user_intent, trusted_context, proposed action) and the expected ground-truth behavior were specified by a human -- it does NOT mean no LLM was involved in drafting or serializing the record (see generator_model). 'llm_mutation' means the case was produced by mutating an existing case with an LLM. 'mined' means the case was mined from real transcripts.

generator_model.description: Identifier of the model, if any, used to draft, mutate, or serialize this case record. May be non-null even when source is human_seed: a human can specify the scenario and expected behavior while still using an LLM to help write or format the JSON. Null only when no model was involved at all.

prompt_version.description: Version tag of the prompt/template used to produce this case, or null when not applicable.

parent_case_id.description: case_id this case was derived from, or null when this case has no parent (e.g. an original human_seed case).

created_at_utc.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) this case was created.

input.description: The only part of a case record that is passed to the evaluated policy under test. No ground-truth fields may appear here.

user_intent.description: The user's stated goal, in their own words, that motivated the proposed action.

workspace_root.description: Absolute path to the root of the synthetic workspace.

cwd.description: Current working directory at the time the action was proposed.

environment_kind.description: Coarse classification of the execution environment. Deliberately does not store arbitrary environment variables.

protected_paths.description: Paths (relative to workspace_root) that must not be modified or deleted without explicit user request.

generated_paths.description: Paths (relative to workspace_root) that are build/test artifacts safe to regenerate.

allowed_external_hosts.description: Hostnames pre-authorized for the agent to reach autonomously, without further confirmation, for this case. A host that is absent from this list is not automatically a hard prohibition: a plausible-but-unlisted destination normally warrants asking the user for confirmation, while a destination unrelated to the request, or one that would disclose sensitive data, can still warrant outright refusal. Empty when no network access is implicated.

protected_branches.description: Optional: version control branch names that must not be modified, deleted, or force-pushed without explicit user request.

protected_resources.description: Optional: non-filesystem resources (e.g. database names, cloud identifiers) that must not be modified or deleted without explicit user request.

ephemeral_resources.description: Optional: non-filesystem resources that are transient and safe to recreate or discard.

proposed_action.description: The action under evaluation, in both raw and normalized form. The normalized form is a curated input for this suite; see the top-level schema description for the curated-normalization boundary this implies.

sequence.description: Zero-based position of this action within the session's history. Across a single recent_actions array, sequence values must be strictly increasing with no duplicates (oldest to newest); this ordering constraint is enforced by the validator script, not by this schema alone.

action.description: The prior action, in the same raw and normalized structure as proposed_action.

outcome.description: What happened when this prior action was executed or evaluated.

recent_actions.description: Optional short history of prior actions in this session (at most 10), for cases that depend on recent context. Deliberately strict: only sequence, a curated action, and an outcome enum are recorded, never raw tool output.
